Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry: target throughput & commit options

Marissa —

Thanks for the intro call earlier. We're interested in Redwood Dedicated for our clinical-document processing pipeline and want to understand committed pool sizing, pricing bands, and how you recommend we structure a reserved commit for the next 12–18 months. High-level on our side:

- Traffic: ~1,200 API requests/minute during peak window (09:00–11:00 PT), baseline ~200/min.
- Payload: median request ~1,000 input tokens; generation ~600 tokens on average. Context length up to 6k tokens in a small % of requests.
- Concurrency: bursty spikes up to ~90 concurrent requests.
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for generation-only calls.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, VPC peering planned.

Attaching a CSV with a simple hourly profile and recent qps snapshots. Can you send a sizing runbook (GPU pool recommendation, assumptions, and cost estimates) and pricing for a committed 12-month and 24-month plan, plus any flexible burst or overage terms? Also would like to know typical lead time for private Dedicated in our us-west region.

Thanks —
Daniel Park
Head of Platform, EchoHealth

Thanks Daniel — good context, appreciate the CSV. Quick clarifying Qs so Ben can run an apples-to-apples sizing: 

1) Are the 1,200 requests/minute measured at the edge (per-minute ingest) or after batching/aggregation at your gateway?
2) Of the 1,200 peak, what percentage do you expect to be generation-heavy (i.e., require full KV cache + long decoding) vs. short completions (few tokens)? Ballpark split is OK (e.g., 70/30).
3) For the 6k token cases: are they primarily single-shot long contexts or streamed multi-call sessions?
4) Do you have a p99 latency goal or just p95 for planning?

Ben — can you put together two pool configs (costed): conservative (headroom for 1.5x peak) and lean (compute for baseline + burst with autoscale) and include expected p95/p99 for the workload described. Also include recommended commit bands (monthly equivalent, 12mo vs 24mo) and sample discount tiers we can offer.

I'll loop in our pricing manager after Ben's note.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity inquiry: target throughput & commit options — sizing calc + options

Daniel / Marissa —

Attached is an initial sizing worksheet and proposal PDF (Redwood_proposal_v2.pdf). Key assumptions and the math below so everything is transparent:

Assumptions from CSV + call:
- Peak ingest: 1,200 rpm = 20 rps; baseline 200 rpm = 3.3 rps.
- Avg tokens handled per request (in + out): 1,600 tokens; median generation 600 tokens.
- Long-context (6k) are ~6% of requests during peak (per CSV).
- Target: p95 gen latency < 350ms; acceptable p99 ~ 700ms for heavy-context cases.

Redwood token throughput guidance (example numbers for our runtime):
- A single A10 GPU (48GB) sustained generation throughput: ~1,200 tokens/sec (seq length dependent).
- H100 (80GB) sustained: ~3,500 tokens/sec for similar batch efficiency.
- Note: long-context (6k) reduces effective tokens/sec ~30% due to KV cache pressure and memory bandwidth.

Sizing options (rounded):
1) Conservative (1.5x peak headroom) — recommend a 4x H100 equivalent pool (we offer this as 8x A10 or 4x H100 SKU mapping). Expected steady peak capacity: ~14k tokens/sec effective (after long-context adjustment). This meets p95 target with room for concurrency; estimated throughput supports ~40 concurrent long jobs or ~220 short completions concurrently.

2) Lean (baseline + autoscale burst) — recommend 3x A10 baseline with autoscale to 6x A10 for peak. Baseline handles ~6k tokens/sec; autoscale to 12k tokens/sec. This reduces committed cost while giving burst coverage.

Pricing & commit guidance (list, example monthly equivalent):
- 12-month reserved (4x H100 equivalent): $68,000/mo list — 20% standard volume discount => $54,400/mo.
- 24-month reserved: $58,000/mo list-equivalent => 25% discount => $43,500/mo.
- Autoscale add-on: metered burst at 1.6x list rate for on-demand capacity beyond reserved.
- Overrun protection: daily throttles or soft overage credits by arrangement.

Flexibility items we can include:
- 12-week ramp schedule with true-up at end of Q1 (reduces upfront commit exposure).
- Annual CPI adjustment capped at 3% for multi-year deals.
- Dedicated SLAs: 99.9% uptime for control plane; latency SLOs by route in the console.

I'll call out tradeoffs in the PDF. If EchoHealth prefers GPU count instead of H100-equivalent abstraction, we can map to exact SKUs and pricing.

Attachments: Redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal with line-item pricing).

—Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)]
